assumptions.choice: Size = floor(available_cash / (current_close * (1 + broker_commission))), read dynamically from self.broker, applied identically to long and short entries
assumptions.reason: Spec requires 100% of capital per trade; this sizing avoids a margin rejection from the commission cost while using the bar's close as the best available price estimate at signal time.

assumptions.choice: Implemented via two CrossOver indicators (RSI vs 30, RSI vs 70): a cross below 30 both arms the long entry and (if short) closes the short; a cross above 70 both arms the short entry and (if long) closes the long; the armed flag is consumed only when flat and the corresponding recovery cross occurs
assumptions.reason: Directly encodes the spec's two-step 'drops below X then rises back above X' entry language and the separate single-step exit language, using only RSI-derived events with no extra filters.

assumptions.choice: Treat Monday-Friday, 09:30-16:00 (bar timestamp) as the valid session; all logic is skipped outside it
assumptions.reason: Spec requires suspending signals/calculation during non-trading periods; exact session bounds aren't stated so standard US equity market hours are used. The supplied hourly feed already contains only in-session bars, so this check is a defensive, literal implementation of the rule rather than an active filter.

assumptions.choice: Ignored the garbled figure '164.00' in the spec's Friday-to-Monday example and treated it as referring to the normal session open
assumptions.reason: The number matches no valid RSI value, price, or time in context and appears to be corrupted text in the source specification.
